nodes.text: ...One moment. A fletch set wrong kills someone eight weeks from now, far from here. There. Now — you have my whole attention, which people tell me is unsettling.

Ten years under Kestrel's banner, walking the High Road with a lamp and a bow. The road gave me back with a knee that predicts weather and a rule I've never broken since: _never send anyone into the dark with gear you wouldn't stake your own life on._ I couldn't walk the miles anymore, so now the miles come to my counter instead. Same oath. Better chair.

The watch on the wall, the castle guard, Kestrel's sergeants, and any honest traveler with coin and sense. The wolfkin dens below the tree line taught this province what a missed shot costs. When a watchman on the night wall nocks one of mine, he's holding my signature. I fletch like their lives depend on it, because I remember when mine did.

Straight grain — the saw yard saves me its best billets and Stig pretends not to be jealous. Feathers matched from the *same wing*, or the arrow corkscrews like a lie unraveling. And patience at the end: the last touch is the one you'll answer for. You can tell a fletcher's character from one arrow. Mine says: slow, and doesn't miss twice.
Fly straight. And thank the goose — everyone forgets the goose.
